chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from Abī Shuʿayb, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥumrān, that he heard a righteous servant say:
Whoever falls asleep while he is sitting, not intending sleep, then no wudu (ablution) is required upon him.

key_terms.لَا يَتَعَمَّدُ: not doing so deliberately or intentionally
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: ritual ablution required for acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Does falling asleep while sitting invalidate wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sleep and wudu (ablution). It indicates that if a person falls asleep while seated without deliberately intending to sleep, his wudu (ablution) is not invalidated.
